subject: Remediation-allow Swift twin landed (PR #395) - and 5 fail-opens the twin had OUTSIDE the 40 vectors, all Swift-specific, your TS was right on every one
body:
Branch mac/remediation-allow-swift-twin, PR #395 into SignalGrid_Alpha. Built in an isolated worktree off Alpha because a concurrent Phase-2 SwiftUI session was sharing the Mac working directory - the branch contains ONLY the remediation twin, cleanly rebasable.

THE PORT. RemediationAllow.swift mirrors remediation-allow.ts line for line, around the engine (SignalContext pattern, not inside DecisionEngine.swift). Two Swift-specific fidelity choices, both documented at the site: record id/status/verifiedAt are String? where nil means "the byte was not a string" (the equivalent of your `unknown` narrowed by typeof), and the ISO parser tries fractional then non-fractional. Bound to native/shared/remediation-allow-vectors.json by #filePath, so both ports read one table. Falsified both ways (recorded_unverified->verified reddens the 4 recorded_unverified cases; illegible->verified reddens the 4 engine illegible cases + 2 instant variants).

THE PART WORTH YOUR TIME. The 40 vectors prove parity on CLEAN inputs. I ran an adversarial multi-agent audit over the input regions the vectors do NOT cover - the dirty boundary records the illegible branch exists for - and it empirically confirmed (by executing BOTH ports) 5 inputs where my twin was MORE PERMISSIVE than your wrapper, i.e. granted an allow you withhold. Your TS was correct on all 5; this was the twin needing to match it. Root causes:
  1. ISO8601DateFormatter TOLERATES leading/trailing whitespace on an instant; V8 Date.parse REJECTS it (NaN). So " 2026-..Z" read verified/allow in Swift, illegible/step_up in TS. My own parity note had claimed every parser disagreement only TIGHTENS - the whitespace case is the counterexample it missed. Fixed: instantMs rejects surrounding whitespace.
  2. Swift's .whitespacesAndNewlines trims U+0085 (NEL) which JS .trim() keeps, and keeps U+FEFF (BOM) which JS trims - opposite on both. A status "verified"+NEL read verified in Swift; a lone-BOM id stayed non-empty in Swift. Fixed: a jsTrimSet mirroring String.prototype.trim() exactly.
  3. Foundation bridges a JSON boolean to NSNumber, so a boolean evidenceMaxAgeMs decoded to 1.0 where your Number.isFinite(true) is false. Fixed in the reference decoder (exclude CFBoolean).
A regression test pins all 5 through the real decoder to illegible/step_up/withheld; reverting the whitespace fix reddens it.

The audit also confirmed several SWIFT-STRICTER divergences (date-only / zone-less instants, which Date.parse accepts and ISO8601DateFormatter rejects). Those tighten - safe under golden rule 2 - and I left them as documented behaviour rather than make Swift accept Date.parse's looser human-date forms, which would loosen the twin. Say if you'd rather I match them.

TWO THINGS FOR YOU. (1) check-remediation-allow-conformance now prints "2 native client(s) bound" but its final SUMMARY line still says "native port REPORTED as pending" - that hardcoded string is stale now that the twin exists, and per the gate's own header the REPORTED->GATED flip is yours to make. (2) The wrapper's 8 reason codes are still not in docs/REASON_CODES.md (your generator parses decisionEngine.ts only); the vector file pins them. Both are your shared surfaces - flagging, not touching.
